counter_evidence:
Two parts of the claim hold. Main has 48 commits whose subject starts with fix or hotfix (git log --oneline main | grep -ciE '^[0-9a-f]+ (fix|hotfix)' returns 48, out of 368 commits on main). The design also does put the audit first: KS-0, decision D1, design doc lines 525-534 and 649-650. What fails is the claim that the audit is a real test.

(1) Recurrence is already visible in git, and it passes the stop rule. Reading the commit bodies of main's own fix commits turns up at least three repeats of the same root cause in separate commits:
- 75b51f9 (07-07, Opus 4.8) then 981ae08 (07-08, Fable 5): mypy --no-implicit-reexport. Same cause, different file, different agent, next day.
- 2f09cec (07-08 10:07, scripts) then f29f62f (07-08 17:58, app entrypoint): NoReferencedTableError because Base.metadata was missing slices. The second one caused a prod login 500.
- b7a5b98 (06-03) then 6928828 (06-26): Expo native modules (expo-asset in both) out of line with the SDK-52 pins, which broke the EAS build.
- A fourth, dbb3661 then d440855 (both 06-08): the same expo-audio stop() IllegalStateException. The first fix (audio focus) was wrong, and d440855's body says it failed.
So a design stop rule of 'stop at 2 or fewer repeats among the 48, counting sibling causes' (D2) cannot fire. X-05.F20's premise of 'almost no explicit repeats' (design line 513) comes from keyword counts on subject lines only.

(2) The 48-commit basis undercounts.
- d440855 and 169ca41 are on main with subjects starting '@ fix(...)', so the regex misses them.
- git log --all finds 72 fix-prefixed commits. 24 of them are not reachable from main because squash merges collapsed them. They include a6f9048, bee11dc ('the selfie finalize is the second head_size caller', a sibling repeat in so many words) and aab2d91 (missing expo-font, a sibling of b7a5b98's missing expo-asset).
- Fixes also land under other prefixes: 140428c (chore) introduced the empty-DSN trap, ee005d1 is 'feat ... repair defects', and ea48987 is the chore that carries migration 0045.

(3) R-02 ex8 is not a re-add, and the audit's basis cannot see it. git log --all -S'@sentry/react-native/expo' -- technician-app/app.json shows the plugin added once (60c026d, feat, 06-10 11:43) and removed on main once (6928828, 06-26). PR #59 merged at 06-10 11:50:59. The fix a6f9048 was committed at 16:04:27 onto the branch that had already been merged, so it never reached main. The 06-26 hit is therefore a re-diagnosis of a fix that never landed. A main-only fix-commit audit cannot pair it, because the first half is a feat commit plus an off-main commit.

(4) Defining a sibling as 'same root cause, different file' with no separate encounter makes one commit enough to break the rule. 2fe77f5 fixes three compare_digest sites (ops deps, messaging router/service) in a single commit, and CLAUDE.md records 'Three sites had exactly that hole'.

(5) Raw repeat counts do not measure escalations avoided. Every repeat above ended once a structural guard went in: the dependabot.yml ignore list, whose comment records the SDK-56 bump; the test_app_bootstrap.py added in f29f62f; CLAUDE.md's Sentry trap; the switch to the expo-av library. The mypy pair diagnoses itself from the error message. Model tier can be recovered (49 of 50 fix commits carry Co-Authored-By trailers), but no cost figure is recorded anywhere. Session-level re-encounters that produced no commit cannot be recovered locally either: ~/.claude/projects holds one jsonl per project folder.

(6) The repo is younger than the claim says. Main's commits run from 2026-05-31 to 2026-08-03, about 9 weeks of activity, not 5 months; X-05.F20's '2026-05-31 and 2026-11-02' is wall-clock time. Production is also moving from Railway to a VPS, so the Railway-specific traps in the history will not recur, and VPS traps have no history to audit.

The 2-repeat threshold does have a defensible basis that the design never states. On a one-sided binomial upper bound (node), 2 of 48 gives 12.5% and 3 of 48 gives 15.4%, so stopping at 2 or fewer works as a necessary-condition test against X-05.F25's illustrative break-even of about 15%. That only holds if the count is of costly, cross-session repeats.
narrowed_claim: Repeats of the same root cause and of sibling causes already exist in this repository's git history. There are at least three in separate commits among main's fix commits, a fourth that the subject regex misses, and more in squash-stripped branch commits and in R-02 ex8's fix that never landed. What is still unproven is whether repeats that would have cost a top-tier escalation, and that happened despite the guards and always-loaded CLAUDE.md that already existed, are frequent enough to clear the about 15% break-even. The design does schedule a git audit first (KS-0/D1). As specified, though (fix-prefixed subjects on main, stop at 2 or fewer repeats counting siblings by file), its basis undercounts and its stop rule is already met, so it cannot stop the track. Until it is redefined, the go/no-go actually rests on the Step 1 blind replay and the Step 2 prospective log.
design_consequence:
Rewrite KS-0 and D2 before the owner rules on them.

1. Basis. Use all refs, not main only (72 fix-prefixed commits, not 48), with the regex fixed for '@ ' subjects. Add reverts and failure-describing feat/chore commits. Pair stranded or unlanded fixes (a6f9048 against 6928828) as re-diagnoses. Capture the PR branches before they are pruned.

2. Unit of count. A repeat is a distinct later encounter of the same root cause. Sibling sites inside one commit (2fe77f5's three compare_digest sites) count once.

3. Weighting. Count only repeats with an opaque or expensive diagnosis that happened while no guard or always-loaded prose covered them. Record the guard installed after each first hit (dependabot ignore, a bootstrap test, a CLAUDE.md trap) as the repository's existing answer to recurrence. That answer is what the store must beat, alongside the grep arm.

4. State the threshold's derivation. 2 of 48 has a 12.5% one-sided upper bound, against the 15% break-even. Admit that the raw sibling-inclusive count already exceeds 2, so KS-0 gives seed and prior data, not a gate. The kill decision belongs to Step 1 and Step 2.

5. Discount the historical prior for the VPS move, because the Railway traps retire and the new traps have no history.

6. Correct the register: R-02 ex8 is one plugin added once (60c026d) whose fix a6f9048 was stranded after PR #59 merged, not a plugin added twice. X-05.F20's 369 commits span 2026-05-31 to 2026-08-03 of activity on main, not 5 months.
